elements.scope_reason: Red-box header: 'Give urgent attention to the traumatised/abused patient with any of' -> Urgent priority anchored on the presenting complaint, (and <complaint> (or ...)).
elements.problem: Urgent level and (and anchor (or items)) structure match the page. Anchor is Victim of abuse OR Victim of psychological trauma; since sexual-assault, physical-assault, emotional-abuse concepts all descend from Victim of abuse, recording any of them satisfies the anchor.
evidence: Urgent: traumatised/abused patient with recent sexual assault, injuries or suicide risk :: adult Urgent (and (or (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Victim of abuse" "finding")) (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Victim of psychological trauma" "finding"))) (or ...))

parts_missing: Time window may not work as intended: the house standard says onset is captured when the finding is recorded, so onset of 'Victim of forced sexual activity' is the recording time, not when the assault happened, unless the worker enters a back-dated onset. In that case the 5-day/3-day limits are always met and any sexual assault, however old, is Urgent
'Victim of rape' (child of Victim of sexual aggression) is not a descendant of 'Victim of forced sexual activity', so a worker who records rape directly does not trigger this branch
elements.problem: Structure is right: (Female AND onset <= 5 days) OR (Male AND onset <= 3 days), with <= used as the house standard's 'within the last N'. Sex is expressed as Female/Male clinical findings in check_for because the grammar has no sex atom, which is acceptable but unusual. Whether this is correct depends on how onset is captured.
evidence: Urgent: ... :: (and (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Female" "finding")) (<= (onset (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Victim of forced sexual activity" "finding"))) (time_ago 5 days)))
Urgent: ... :: (and (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Male" "finding")) (<= (onset (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Victim of forced sexual activity" "finding"))) (time_ago 3 days)))

parts_missing: 'needing attention' is dropped: any Traumatic injury, even a minor one that has been dealt with, makes the patient Urgent
elements.problem: 'Injuries needing attention' is encoded as plain Traumatic injury with no qualifier, so the rule over-triggers. No precoordinated 'injury requiring attention' concept exists, but a qualifier (such as Current, or a severity) would match the page more closely.

All four parts are encoded: suicidal thoughts -> Suicidal thoughts; plans -> Planning suicide; overdose -> Overdose (disorder); self harm -> Self-injurious behavior. 'Intentional overdose' would be closer to the page's suicide-risk context, but the broader Overdose is safe for triage.

elements.scope_reason: Bullet 1 'Suspect abuse if ...' -> possible Victim of abuse. Bullet 2 (safe space, confidentiality, record account) is a management_step and is not judged.
parts_missing: patient discloses: only indirect, because recording Victim of abuse is a due_to of the check task; there is no evidence in the possible rule
elements.problem: The possible 'Victim of abuse' rule uses only 'Abnormal behavior' (behaviour seems strange). Abnormal behavior is very broad, so it will raise possible abuse, and so the abuse check task, for any patient with abnormal behaviour. That may be acceptable as a pre-screen.
evidence: Diagnose possible abuse (traumatised/abused patient page) :: (diagnosis (snomed_concept "Victim of abuse" "finding") possible) adult (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Abnormal behavior" "finding"))

elements.scope_reason: Abuse row: three 'X likely' bullets (probable rules) and one 'consider other types of abuse' bullet (possible rule). 'Document on J88' is a management step.
parts_missing: Bullet 1 (sexual assault/rape likely): correct. Victim of forced sexual activity -> probable Victim of sexual aggression

Bullet 2 (physical abuse likely): history of physical assault, old/new scars and bruises are encoded; 'unusual wounds' is missing; 'bruises of different ages' is encoded as Multiple bruising, which loses 'different ages'

Bullet 3 (emotional/verbal/psychological abuse likely): harassment, being ridiculed/controlled and insulted are all missing (Victim of verbal abuse and Victim of bullying exist); threatened -> Victim of threats is correct; excessively withdrawn/fearful/anxious is correct with the Severe qualifier

Bullet 3: 'intimidation' is encoded as 'Intimidation' (finding), whose parent is Aggressive behavior. It means the patient intimidates others, not that the patient is a victim of intimidation, so the concept is wrong
Bullet 3: the diagnosis 'Victim of emotional abuse' covers only emotional abuse; its siblings Victim of verbal abuse and Victim of psychological abuse exist and are not concluded
Bullet 4 ('consider other types of abuse' for other unwelcome behaviour, manipulation or violation): no possible rule at all
elements.problem: Sexual assault is complete. Physical and emotional abuse are partial, with one wrong concept (Intimidation). 'Consider other types of abuse' is missing. Both probable rules also require Victim of abuse or Victim of psychological trauma, which the page does not say, though in practice the evidence concepts (Victim of physical assault) satisfy the anchor themselves.
evidence: Diagnose probable sexual assault/rape :: (diagnosis (snomed_concept "Victim of sexual aggression" "finding") probable) adult (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Victim of forced sexual activity" "finding"))

Diagnose probable physical abuse :: (and (or Victim of abuse | Victim of psychological trauma) (or (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Victim of physical assault" "finding")) (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Scar" "disorder")) (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Multiple bruising" "finding"))))

rule_level_problems.rule: Urgent: traumatised/abused patient with recent sexual assault, injuries or suicide risk
rule_level_problems.problem: The 5-day/3-day window relies on the onset of 'Victim of forced sexual activity'. If onset defaults to the recording time (as the house standard describes), the window is always met at triage, so old assaults are also Urgent. The rules need the assault time captured as onset, or a note in remaining questions.

Uses 'Intimidation' (finding; child of Aggressive behavior), which describes the patient's own behaviour, not being intimidated. The concept is wrong, and the same finding sits in the check_for list, so the health worker is asked whether the patient is intimidating.

The page's 'consider other types of abuse' (any other unwelcome behaviour, manipulation or violation) has no possible rule. The emotional-abuse rule also leaves out harassment, ridicule/control and insults, and concludes only emotional abuse, not verbal or psychological abuse.
'Injuries needing attention' is encoded as any Traumatic injury, so a minor or already-treated injury in an abused patient becomes Urgent. Over-triage.
Lacks 'unusual wounds'. Also, 'Victim of rape' and 'Victim of sexual aggression' descend from 'Victim of physical assault', so a recorded rape also yields probable physical abuse.

rule_level_problems.rule: Check for traumatised/abused patient urgent signs and abuse type
rule_level_problems.problem: Sex is checked as Female/Male clinical findings because there is no sex atom. The check list and the priority rule agree, and every check_for item is used by a rule.

summary: The red box is encoded with the right Urgent level and all items, but the 5-day/3-day sexual-assault window depends on onset being the assault time rather than the recording time, and 'injuries needing attention' has lost its 'needing attention' limit. Among the 'likely' rules, emotional/verbal/psychological abuse uses the wrong concept for intimidation (the patient's own aggressive behaviour), leaves out harassment, ridicule and insults, and concludes only emotional abuse; physical abuse lacks unusual wounds, and 'consider other types of abuse' has no rule. The 'suspect abuse' possible rule covers only strange behaviour.
